craft_notes: Sthāyin: ordered precondition — the vidhi opens by declaring its own order (FIRST unit: sets the house voice; owner verdict required). Sanskrit-first: vaktavyam gerundive kept passive (must-be-told); prāk + kartavyam order kept: nature-set-forth AFTER bath-taught. Rows: 1 (first…taught: the instruction's sequence IS the line-break), 6 (iti-uktaṃ 'it is said' anchors the declaration verbatim), 12 (śānta-close: the bath lands, nothing yet performed). Close: 'the to-be-done bath is taught.' Rejected: opening with the bath — killed: prāk order is the argument; 'shall be expounded' for told — killed: vaktavyam kept must-be-told. Read aloud: IN-i-ti-a-TION and-the-REST must-be-TOLD — it-is-SAID; SO-to-SET-forth IN-i-ti-a-TION's NA-ture, FIRST the-TO-be-DONE BATH is-TAUGHT.

lines: Initiation and the rest must be told — it is said;
so to set forth initiation's nature, first
l4.sanskrit_cite: dīkṣādikaṃ vaktavyam iti uktam ato dīkṣāsvarūpanirūpaṇārthaṃ prāk kartavyaṃ snānam upadiśyate

reads_against.argmap: Why is the bath taught before initiation? → The bath is the precondition of the exposition: initiation's nature is set forth by first teaching the bath to be performed.
c1_essence: Initiation's nature is set forth through the bath: the to-be-done bath is taught first.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vidhi weight (quiescence carrying ritual order)
